source_text: Ἀλλ᾿ ἵνα καὶ εὐγνωμονέστερον αὐτῷ δῶμεν ἃ μὴ ἑώρακεν ἀπὸ τῶν ἐν τῇ Γενέσει γεγραμμένων. ὅτι „ἰδόντες οἱ υἱοὶ τοῦ θεοῦ τὰς θυγατέρας τῶν ἀνθρώπων ὅτι καλαί εἰσιν, ἔλαβον ἑαυτοῖς γυναῖκας ἀπὸ πασῶν ὧν ἐξελέξαντο“· οὐδὲν ἧττον καὶ περὶ τούτων τοῖς δυναμένοις ἀκούειν προφητικοῦ βουλήματος πείσομεν ὅτι καὶ τῶν πρὸ ἡμῶν τις ταῦτα ἀνήγαγεν εἰς τὸν περὶ ψυχῶν λόγον, ἐν ἐπιθυμίᾳ γενομένων τοῦ· ἐν σώματι ἀνθρώπων βίου. ἅπερ τροπολογῶν ἔφασκε λελέχθαι „θυγατέρας ἀνθρώπων.“ πλὴν ὅπως ποτ᾿ ἂν ἔχῃ καὶ τὰ περὶ τοὺς ἐπιθυμήσαντας θυγατέρων ἀνθρώπων υἱοὺς θεῶν, οὐδὲν αὐτῷ συμβάλλεται ὁ λόγος πρὸς τὸ μὴ μόνον τὸν Ἰησοῦν ὡς ἄγγελον ἐπιδεδημηκέναι τοῖς ἀνθρώποις, σωτῆρα καὶ εὐεργέτην ἐναργῶς πάντων τῶν μεταβαλλόντων ἀπὸ τῆς χύσεως τῆς κακίας γεγενημένον. εἶτα φύρων καὶ συγχέων ἃ ὅπως ποτὲ ἤκουσε καὶ τὰ ὅπου ποτ᾿ οὖν γεγραμμένα, εἴτε δεδογμένα θεῖα εἶναι παρὰ Χριστιανοῖς εἴτε καὶ μὴ, φησὶ τοὺς ὁμοῦ καταβεβηκότας ἑξήκοντα ἢ ἑβδομήκοντα κολάζεσθαι δεσμοῖς ὑποβληθέντας ἐν γῇ. καὶ φέρει ὡς ἀπὸ τοῦ Ἐνὼχ, οὐκ ὀνομάζων αὐτὸν, τό· ὅθεν καὶ τὰς θερμὰς πηγὰς εἶναι τὰ ἐκείνων δάκρυα, πρᾶγμα οὔτε λεγόμενον οὔτ᾿ ἀκουόμενον ἐν ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις τοῦ θεοῦ. οὐδὲ γὰρ ἀνόητος οὕτως τις ἦν. ἵνα σωματοποιήσῃ δάκρυα παραπλήσια τοῖς τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἐν τοῖς καταβεβηκόσιν ἐξ οὐρανοῦ ἀγγέλοις. καὶ εἰ χρή γε παίζειν πρὸς τὰ καθ᾿ ἡμῶν σπουδαζόμενα τῷ Κέλσῳ, λεκτέον ὅτι οὐκ ἄν τις εἶπε τὰς θερμὰς πηγὰς, ὧν αἱ πλεῖσται γλυκεῖαί εἰσι, δάκρυα εἶναι τῶν ἀγγέλων, ἐπεὶ ἡ φύσις τῶν δακρύων ἐστὶν ἁλμυρά· εἰ μὴ ἄρα οἱ κατὰ τὸν Κέλσον ἄγγελοι γλυκέα δακρύουσιν.
thought_title: The sons of God and the tears of angels
pass_a_gloss: But in order that we may grant (δίδωμι) him even more generously (εὐγνωμονέστερον) what he has not seen from the things written in Genesis, that 'the sons of God, seeing the daughters of men that they are beautiful (καλαί), took for themselves wives from all whom they chose (ἐκλέγομαι)': none the less about these things too we shall persuade those able to hear a prophetic intention (προφητικὸν βούλημα) that one of those before us led these things up (ἀνάγω) to the account (λόγος) about souls (ψυχαί) that came into desire (ἐπιθυμία) of the life (βίος) of men in a body; which things, speaking figuratively (τροπολογέω), he said were called 'daughters of men'. However it may be with the sons of gods who desired daughters of men, the account contributes (συμβάλλομαι) nothing to him toward Jesus not alone having visited men as an angel, he having become evidently (ἐναργῶς) Saviour and benefactor (εὐεργέτης) of all who change (μεταβάλλω) from the pouring-out (χύσις) of wickedness (κακία). Then mixing (φύρω) and confusing (συγχέω) the things he heard however, and the things written wherever, whether held (δοκέω) to be divine among Christians or not, he says those who came down (καταβαίνω) together sixty or seventy are punished being subjected to bonds in the earth. And he brings as from Enoch, not naming him, the 'whence also the hot springs are their tears', a thing neither said nor heard in the churches of God. For no one was so foolish (ἀνόητος) as to make bodily (σωματοποιέω) tears like those of men in the angels who came down from heaven. And if one must jest (παίζω) toward the things earnestly pursued (σπουδάζω) against us by Celsus, it must be said that no one would have said the hot springs, of which most are sweet (γλυκεῖαι), are tears of the angels, since the nature of tears is salty (ἁλμυρά); unless perhaps the angels according to Celsus weep (δακρύω) sweet things.

pass_b_english: But let us be more generous and grant him what he did not see in what is written in Genesis, that “the sons of God, seeing that the daughters of men were beautiful, took wives for themselves from all whom they chose” (Genesis 6:2). Even so, we shall persuade those who can hear the intention of prophecy that about these things too one of those before us referred these words to the teaching about souls, souls that had come to desire the life of men in the body; and he said, interpreting figuratively, that this is what is meant by “daughters of men.” Yet however things may stand with the sons of God who desired the daughters of men, the passage does nothing to help Celsus show that Jesus was not the only one to have visited men as an angel, Jesus, who has plainly become the Saviour and benefactor of all who turn away from the flood of wickedness.

Then, mixing up and confusing what he heard, however he heard it, and things written wherever they were written, whether held by Christians to be divine or not, he says that the sixty or seventy who came down together are punished by being put in bonds in the earth. And he cites as from Enoch, though without naming him, the words “that is why the hot springs are their tears,” a thing neither said nor heard in the churches of God. For no one was so foolish as to give the angels who came down from heaven bodily tears like those of men. And if we must jest in answer to what Celsus labours at so earnestly against us, it must be said that no one would have called the hot springs, most of which are sweet, the tears of the angels, since the nature of tears is salty; unless, of course, Celsus's angels weep sweet tears.
notes: Genesis 6:2 is quoted in the Septuagint wording (ἰδόντες ... οἱ υἱοὶ τοῦ θεοῦ τὰς θυγατέρας τῶν ἀνθρώπων ὅτι καλαί εἰσιν ...). 'One of those before us' is unnamed; the soul-reading matches Philo, On the Giants 6–18, but Origen does not name him, so this is a probable identification only. ἅπερ τροπολογῶν ἔφασκε λελέχθαι 'θυγατέρας ἀνθρώπων': ἅπερ is neuter plural with a vague antecedent (human bodies or bodily life); rendered 'this is what is meant'. The staged text has a stray raised point in τοῦ· ἐν σώματι, ignored. υἱοὺς θεῶν ('sons of gods') in the staged text is rendered 'sons of God' to match the Genesis quotation just given; θεῶν may be a slip for θεοῦ, or Origen may echo Celsus's pagan idiom; flagged as a doubtful reading. γλυκεῖαι: 'sweet' (fresh) water, kept as 'sweet' for both clauses to keep Origen's joke. χύσις τῆς κακίας: 'flood' (pouring-out) of wickedness. Full stops after γεγραμμένων and ἦν in the staged text break single sentences; read as running on. Review: Genesis 6:2 checked against the LXX wording (exact). 'ever' dropped (not in οὐδὲ ... ἦν); σωματοποιήσῃ ... ἐν τοῖς ... ἀγγέλοις recast in natural order; ψυχῶν ... γενομένων made explicit as the souls that desired bodily life. The υἱοὺς θεῶν reading stays flagged; the owner may wish to check Koetschau's apparatus.

Open doubt (review): 5.55: the staged text reads υἱοὺς θεῶν ('sons of gods'). It is rendered 'sons of God' to match Genesis 6:2 and flagged in translator_notes. It is worth checking Koetschau's apparatus. The verdict is pass, because the English is right under either reading.
